mechanism_narrative: A rise in GDP above its 6-month moving average indicates increased economic activity, leading to higher demand for goods and services, which in turn drives up S&P 500 prices over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of GDP growth above its 6-month moving average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5%, it signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, which in turn drives down S&P 500 prices over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when the federal funds rate exceeds 5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 5% indicates a weakening labor market, leading to decreased consumer spending and lower S&P 500 prices over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when the unemployment rate exceeds 5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) both increase, it indicates a strong demand for goods and services, leading to higher S&P 500 prices over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when both housing starts and retail sales increase (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 3-month moving average indicates increased supply, leading to higher S&P 500 prices over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when industrial production increases above its 3-month moving average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) both increase, it indicates a tightening monetary policy and increased inflation, leading to lower S&P 500 prices over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when both the federal funds rate and the consumer price index increase (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate below 4% indicates a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and higher S&P 500 prices over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when the unemployment rate is below 4% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) both increase, it indicates a strong demand for goods and services, leading to higher S&P 500 prices over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when both GDP and housing starts increase (t-test p > 0.05).
